title: Code Reviews and Team Collaboration knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a production-oriented TypeScript project demonstrate?
options: Secrets committed into client bundles for convenience.
Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
Type annotations as a replacement for authorization and validation.
A working happy path without tests or documentation.
questions.answer_key: Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires runtime, security, testing and operational evidence beyond type checking.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Code Reviews and Team Collaboration”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with reviewing public type contracts and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with reviewing public type contracts and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Reviewing public type contracts”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Code Reviews and Team Collaboration”?
options: Assume version control and collaborative workflows is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check shared style and linting rules, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check shared style and linting rules, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Shared style and linting rules”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
